benchmark.timing: Seconds include opening the dataset and executing the action, excluding interpreter/JVM startup. Engines ran sequentially. The host was shared with other development work. These four cases do not establish universal performance parity.

implementation.python: API wrappers only; no Python row decoding or row/entry materialization.
rust: Metadata and reference schemas, compressed block streaming, direct Arrow column builders.
Independent DataFusion file partitions with backpressure, cancellation and surfaced worker errors.
Vortex LayoutReader with filter/projection evaluation and live-range decoding reuse.
Separate Hail B-tree index readers for directory metadata and inline metadata footers.
Generic indexed row-ordinal slices seek directly to virtual block offsets.
Single integer-key filters prune partition bounds and seek indexed sub-file ranges.
Metadata-backed counts preserve original Hail partition counts.
Matrix rows and entries align as bounded native batches; globals and column axes materialize in Rust.
scope: Only local paths and file URIs, as in the previous migration reader.
Automatic key-index predicate pushdown currently supports single Int32/Int64 keys. Unsupported predicates retain residual DataFusion filtering and streaming reads.
Row-ordinal index slices support other decoded key types without comparing keys.
Files without usable indexes scan sequentially to find row boundaries.
Original observable Hail partitions are preserved; the reader exposes independent row slices but does not introduce a distributed scheduler or automatically change public partition counts.
Batches have row limits and the streaming decoder has an advisory byte target. Exact Vortex row-range batches can exceed that byte target for wide rows.
Nested demand analysis skips unused root columns; it conservatively decodes complete selected nested columns.
